Diff two vectors

Source: R/diff.R
diff_vec.Rd

Computes the shortest edit script that turns old into new: which runs of old are kept, deleted or inserted.

Usage

diff_vec(old, new, algorithm = c("myers", "patience"), max_cost = NULL)

Arguments

old, new

Two vectors of the same type: logical, integer, double, complex, character or raw. A factor counts as a character vector of its labels.

algorithm

The diff algorithm: "myers", the default, or "patience". Myers finds a shortest edit script. Patience first aligns the elements that occur exactly once on each side, then diffs the stretches between them, with Myers where a stretch has no such element. On text it keeps functions and blocks aligned where Myers may match stray braces and blank lines instead. Its scripts are not minimal in general, and the result always records minimal = FALSE.

max_cost

The cost limit of Myers' search, which trades minimality for time. NULL, the default, follows GNU diff: about the square root of the input size, and at least 4096. Inf always finds a minimal script, in O((N + M) D) time for edit distance D. A smaller number gives up sooner on very different inputs; the script is still correct, but may not be minimal, which the result records.

The limit counts the steps of each middle-snake search, as GNU diff does, not the edit distance of the whole script.

Value

An object of class zudiff. Read it with diff_edits() and diff_identical(), and apply it with diff_apply().

Details

Two elements are equal when match() says so: NA equals NA, NaN equals NaN but not NA, 0 equals -0, strings compare after translation to a common encoding, and factors compare by label. Doubles compare exactly; round them first for a tolerance, for example diff_vec(round(x, 6), round(y, 6)). Raw vectors are compared byte by byte.

Examples

d <- diff_vec(c("a", "b", "c"), c("a", "x", "c"))
diff_edits(d)
#>       op old_start old_len new_start new_len
#> 1  equal         1       1         1       1
#> 2 delete         2       1         2       0
#> 3 insert         3       0         2       1
#> 4  equal         3       1         3       1
